It links the compactness of a hierarchical structure with the efficient traversal and trilinear/quadrilinear filtering capabilities of regular grids on GPU [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the evidence links the compactness of a hierarchical structure with efficient traversal and trilinear/quadrilinear filtering capabilities of regular grids on GPU. Source [S1] explicitly states in the 'Présentation' section: 'Cette structure permet de lier les avantages d'une structure hiérarchique en terme de compacité des données à ceux d'une grille régulière lors du parcours sur GPU.' Additionally, the notes mention that the structure combines an N3-tree for hierarchy with regular voxel bricks, and the bricks allow for trilinear filtering (mentioned in the context of the 1-voxel border and hardware filtering). Thus, all facts in the claim are present in the evidence.

*   **Output:** A GPU-accessible structure consisting of an indirection texture (the tree), a brick storage texture (the data), and a brick indirection storage (mip-level mapping) [S1, unofficial].

The claim accurately reflects the details provided in Source [S1]. The source describes a two-level hierarchical structure (N3-tree) for procedural volume exploration. It specifies that the tree is stored in an indirection texture (3D texture with GL_RGBA32I_EXT format), the data is stored in a brick storage texture (regular voxel bricks), and there is a 'brick indirection storage' that links the tree to the brick data, specifically managing addresses for mip-mapping levels. All components mentioned in the claim (indirection texture, brick storage texture, brick indirection storage) are explicitly described in the source text.

*   **Cell Encoding (Sub-node information):** Each cell contains 32 bits packed as follows [S1, unofficial]:

The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly confirms every detail of the claim. It states that the indirection storage uses a 3D texture with GL_RGBA32I_EXT format (32 bits per component). It details the encoding: Red (R) contains the 3D address (X, Y, Z) of the child node or brick, Green (G) contains the parent node address, Blue (B) is reserved, and Alpha (A) stores the average voxel value. It specifies that 10 bits are used per coordinate (30 bits total), plus 1 bit for sub-node type and 1 bit for the empty node flag, totaling 32 bits. It also mentions the maximum addressable dimension of 1024^3 due to the 10-bit address.
supported

The evidence explicitly states in the notes and the French text that within the 32-bit sub-node encoding, '1 bit allows identifying the sub-node type (brick or tree node)' and '1 bit allows identifying an empty node and without descendants.' This matches the claim exactly.

Source [S1] explicitly states in the notes and passages: 'Implement 3D mip-mapping manually rather than using GPU hardware mip-mapping... The N3-tree with regular mipmapped bricks is a two-level hierarchical data structure for procedural volume exploration that combines an N-ary tree (N3-tree) for hierarchy with regular voxel bricks stored in the leaves [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the N3-tree with regular mipmapped bricks is a two-level hierarchical data structure for procedural volume exploration that combines an N-ary tree (N3-tree) for hierarchy with regular voxel bricks stored in the leaves. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in section 3.3.2: 'La structure que nous avons développée se décompose en deux niveaux : une structure hiérarchique en N3 -tree ... formant une structure d'arbre à N3 fils et des briques de données régulières stockées dans les feuilles de cette structure.' It also mentions it is for 'procedural volume exploration' (implied by the context of rendering and traversal on GPU) and combines the compactness of the hierarchy with the efficient traversal of regular grids.
